kettleMaterials.name: 316 Surgical-Grade Stainless Steel (18/10/2 Cr-Ni-Mo) – Concealed Base
kettleMaterials.alloyDesignation: UNS S31600 / EN 1.4401 (18% Cr, 10% Ni, 2% Mo, balance Fe)
kettleMaterials.snasAllergyRisk: Safe / Non-Reactive (Safe for severe nickel contact allergy & SNAS)
kettleMaterials.passivationDurability: Superior. 2% Molybdenum addition creates a self-healing chromium-molybdenum oxide passive film resistant to chlorides and mild food acids.
kettleMaterials.description: Medical and high-purity laboratory grade stainless steel. Submerged heating plate is protected against chloride pitting and acid etching, ensuring trace metal migration remains far below drinking water guidelines.

kettleMaterials.name: 304 Food-Grade Stainless Steel (18/8 Cr-Ni) – Concealed Flat Base
kettleMaterials.alloyDesignation: UNS S30400 / EN 1.4301 (18% Cr, 8% Ni, balance Fe)
kettleMaterials.whoCompliance: Compliant under normal fresh-pour use (<20 µg/L limit)
kettleMaterials.euDirectiveCompliance: Compliant for fresh water; can exceed limit if water stands overnight
kettleMaterials.snasAllergyRisk: Low for fresh boils; moderate risk if water is left stagnant overnight
kettleMaterials.passivationDurability: Good. Forms protective Cr2O3 passive layer, but susceptible to micro-pitting in hard tap water with chlorides (>100 ppm) or low pH (<6.5).
kettleMaterials.description: The standard alloy for quality domestic electric kettles. Delivers safe performance when freshly boiled and discarded after use, but prolonged water stagnation drives measurable nickel migration into solution.

kettleMaterials.name: Borosilicate Glass Body with Concealed 304 Stainless Base
kettleMaterials.alloyDesignation: Schott Duran / Borosilicate 3.3 Walls + 304 Stainless Disc Bottom
kettleMaterials.elementConfig: Concealed Flat Stainless Heating Base with Inert Glass Walls
kettleMaterials.euDirectiveCompliance: Fully Compliant across all test conditions
kettleMaterials.snasAllergyRisk: Minimal (55% reduction in wetted metal surface area vs all-steel kettle)
kettleMaterials.passivationDurability: High. Inert non-porous glass walls eliminate metal ion dissolution from side walls; provides 100% visual visibility for early limescale detection.
kettleMaterials.description: Hybrid design pairing non-reactive thermal shock-resistant glass walls with a flat stainless bottom heating plate. Reduces total metallic contact surface area by more than half and provides clear visual feedback on scale buildup.

kettleMaterials.name: 201 Low-Nickel / High-Manganese Stainless Steel (Budget Import)
kettleMaterials.alloyDesignation: AISI 201 / 1Cr17Mn6Ni5N (16% Cr, 3.5% Ni, 6.5% Mn, balance Fe)
kettleMaterials.whoCompliance: Borderline / High Non-Compliance Risk (>20 µg/L in warm/standing water)
kettleMaterials.euDirectiveCompliance: Fails EU Specific Release Limits when exposed to warm acidic tea water
kettleMaterials.snasAllergyRisk: High (Manganese and nickel co-leaching trigger contact dermatitis and dysbiosis)
kettleMaterials.passivationDurability: Poor. Manganese substitution destabilizes the austenite matrix, causing rapid localized pinhole pitting, rust halos, and rough micro-fissures within 3–6 months.
kettleMaterials.description: Used in ultra-low-cost bargain kettles to save manufacturing costs. Lacks adequate nickel and molybdenum, causing the thin chromium barrier to break down rapidly under repeated thermal cycling and hard mineral attack.

kettleMaterials.name: Vintage / Cheap Travel Kettle Exposed Immersion Element (Nickel-Plated Copper)
kettleMaterials.alloyDesignation: Nickel-Plated Copper Tubing with Silver/Copper Brazed Joint Bushings
kettleMaterials.elementConfig: Exposed Raw Helical Coil Submerged in Water Chamber
kettleMaterials.whoCompliance: Severe Failure (Exceeds WHO 20 µg/L threshold by 2.5x to 6x)
kettleMaterials.euDirectiveCompliance: Illegal for New Sale under Modern EU Food Contact Directives
kettleMaterials.snasAllergyRisk: Critical / Hazardous (Severe trigger for systemic nickel allergy syndrome)
kettleMaterials.passivationDurability: Critically Defective. Direct high-temperature water contact (coil core reaches >250°C) combined with brazing flux seams causes aggressive galvanic corrosion and heavy metal dissolution.
kettleMaterials.description: Legacy and budget travel immersion elements. The bare coiled metal operates at extreme surface temperatures directly in the water column. Thermal expansion micro-cracks the plating, dumping toxic nickel and copper ions into hot water.

waterHardnessTiers.name: Soft Water (<60 ppm CaCO3 / <3.5 gpg)
waterHardnessTiers.thermalImpact: Negligible. Heating element remains bare and thermally coupled to liquid water.
waterHardnessTiers.description: Found in rain-fed municipal water or home reverse osmosis / ion-exchange softened water. Minimal mineral crust, though naturally soft acidic water can slightly increase initial metal ion dissolution.

waterHardnessTiers.name: Moderately Hard Water (60–120 ppm CaCO3 / 3.5–7.0 gpg)
waterHardnessTiers.thermalImpact: Low. Light mineral dusting forms on heating disc without significant thermal impedance.
waterHardnessTiers.description: Standard municipal water in balanced aquifer zones. Forms a fine calcium carbonate dusting that acts as a partial protective barrier against metal leaching without degrading boil efficiency.

waterHardnessTiers.name: Hard Water (120–200 ppm CaCO3 / 7.0–11.7 gpg)
waterHardnessTiers.thermalImpact: Moderate to High. Forms a 0.5–1.0 mm insulating crust within 100–150 boils, creating loud kettle rumble.
waterHardnessTiers.description: Limestone and chalk bedrock regions. Calcium bicarbonate decomposes during boiling into insoluble calcium carbonate crust, insulating the element and increasing power consumption.

waterHardnessTiers.name: Very Hard Water (>200–350+ ppm CaCO3 / >11.7–20+ gpg)
waterHardnessTiers.thermalImpact: Severe. Thick 1.5–3.0 mm calcite crust decouples heating plate, overheating core element to >250°C.
waterHardnessTiers.description: Deep well and highly mineralized tap water. Heavy porous limescale causes severe thermal decoupling, nuisance false-trips of the bimetal boil switch, and under-deposit galvanic pitting.

waterDwellTimes.name: Freshly Boiled & Immediately Poured (<2 minutes)
waterDwellTimes.exposureRisk: Minimum. Metal contact occurs only during the active 3-minute heating cycle.
waterDwellTimes.description: Water is filled cold, brought to rolling boil, and immediately dispensed into mug or teapot. Minimal residence time for passive metal leaching.

waterDwellTimes.name: Left Warm in Kettle for 2 Hours
waterDwellTimes.exposureRisk: Low to Moderate. Warm water accelerates ionic diffusion across stainless surface.
waterDwellTimes.description: Boiled water remains in kettle cooling from 95°C to 45°C. Elevated temperature promotes continued ionic dissolution of surface nickel.

waterDwellTimes.name: Stagnant Water Re-Boiled Morning After (8–12 Hours Overnight)
waterDwellTimes.exposureRisk: High. Overnight stagnation allows extensive galvanic leaching; re-boiling concentrates ions.
waterDwellTimes.description: Common kitchen habit: re-boiling leftover kettle water from the previous evening. Prolonged room-temperature contact leaches heavy metals, and evaporation during re-boil concentrates ppm.

waterDwellTimes.name: Stagnant Water Left 48+ Hours (Weekend Stagnation)
waterDwellTimes.exposureRisk: Critical. Long dwell establishes oxygen concentration cells, driving localized pitting and heavy metal release.
waterDwellTimes.description: Unemptied kettle left over a weekend. Creates differential aeration cells that attack passive metal boundaries, dumping concentrated nickel, iron, and chromium into the liquid.

descalingProtocols.name: Food-Grade Citric Acid (2%–5% Solution) [Gold Standard]
descalingProtocols.chemistry: Forms highly soluble calcium citrate chelation complex: 3CaCO3 + 2C6H8O7 -> Ca3(C6H5O7)2 + 3CO2 + 3H2O
descalingProtocols.passivationImpact: Protective. Does not attack chromium oxide (Cr2O3) passivation; restores clean metallic sheen.
descalingProtocols.odorFlavorResidue: Zero odor. Odorless, biodegradable, rinses clean in a single cold water flush.
descalingProtocols.gasketSafety: 100% safe on EPDM and silicone internal lid and temperature sensor gaskets.
descalingProtocols.description: The safest, most effective descaling agent recommended by appliance manufacturers and materials scientists. Dissolves calcite rapidly without etching metal or imparting pungent smells.

descalingProtocols.name: White Distilled Vinegar (5% Acetic Acid - Boiled Hot)
descalingProtocols.chemistry: Acetic acid reaction: CaCO3 + 2CH3COOH -> Ca(CH3COO)2 + CO2 + H2O
descalingProtocols.passivationImpact: Aggressive / Etching. Boiled acetic acid dissolves the Cr2O3 passive film, causing temporary 3x–6x spike in nickel leaching during the next 3–5 boils!
descalingProtocols.odorFlavorResidue: Pungent volatile acetic vapors; leaves persistent sour smell requiring 3 to 5 wasted boil-and-dump flushes.
descalingProtocols.gasketSafety: Degrades rubber and synthetic gaskets over repeated cycles, causing premature brittleness and leaks.
descalingProtocols.description: Popular home remedy with serious drawbacks. Hot acetic acid strips the protective chromium barrier from stainless steel, dramatically accelerating nickel leaching into subsequently boiled water until re-passivated.

descalingProtocols.name: Mechanical Scrubbing with Wire Wool / Abrasive Scourer
descalingProtocols.chemistry: Physical gouging and mechanical shear across stainless heating disc
descalingProtocols.passivationImpact: Destructive. Gouges micro-scratches into metal, embedding iron debris and exposing non-passivated alloy grains. Permanently elevates nickel leaching.
descalingProtocols.odorFlavorResidue: No chemical odor, but sheds microscopic steel particulates into drinking water.
descalingProtocols.gasketSafety: High risk of tearing silicone base-seal gasket leading to electrical short circuit.
descalingProtocols.description: Severely damaging to electric kettles. Scratches destroy the uniform mirror-polished factory passivation, creating millions of microscopic crevice sites where corrosion and heavy metal leaching occur perpetually.

descalingProtocols.name: No Descaling (Untreated Heavy Limescale Accumulation)
descalingProtocols.chemistry: Continuous crystallization of CaCO3, MgCO3, and silica into porous insulating ceramic layer
descalingProtocols.passivationImpact: Under-deposit corrosion. Scale traps moisture and chlorides against metal surface, starving it of oxygen and inducing localized pitting corrosion.
descalingProtocols.odorFlavorResidue: Chalky mineral taste, floating white scale flakes in tea and coffee.
descalingProtocols.gasketSafety: Crust expands into gasket crevices, forcing seam separation and base leaks.
descalingProtocols.description: Untreated scale acts as a thermal blanket, forcing the heating element to run hundreds of degrees hotter than design specs. Traps stagnant moisture underneath, accelerating anaerobic crevice pitting.
